intelligence.human_view: A button that does nothing is the same failure as the picker that switches nothing (SN-3001 My World Picker Must Switch) — a control that performs its own performance instead of its job. The Create world modal performs twice over: it looks like a form (flat buttons, plain text) and it acts like a dead end (tap create, nothing happens, nowhere to go). His correction has two halves and both are absolute. First, the look: "not flat buttons all depth and nice and primo" — the design law is a habit, and a modal is a human surface, so its buttons are real objects with real depth, not flat shapes. Second, the deed: creating a world must actually create the feed and show you the feed, optimized to that world — the tap builds the world and takes you into it, tuned to that world, in the same motion. "It never just goes nowhere" is the rule in its shortest form: a create action that creates nothing is not a create action. The verification is the tap itself, like the picker's: create a world, and you are standing in that world's feed — proven on the page, not asserted in a brief.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you have a magic button that says "MAKE A WORLD!" — you press it, and... NOTHING happens! No world appears! That's not a magic button at all! A real magic button makes the world AND takes you right into it, so you can see it and play in it! And the button shouldn't be flat and boring — it should be big and shiny and pop right out, like a real button you want to press!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine a button that says "make a world," dear, and when you press it, nothing happens at all! Oh, love — that's not a button, that's a picture of a button! A real button does its job, dear — you press it, and there is your world, all made and waiting for you, lovely and just for you. And the button itself should be beautiful, love — not flat and dull, but deep and rich, a real thing you want to press.
intelligence.naya_view: Create world must actually create. The pop-up looks flat and boring, and when you tap create it goes nowhere. Buttons with all depth, nice and primo — and when you create a world it actually builds that world's feed and shows it to you, tuned to that world. It never just goes nowhere.
